prompt: Challenge C124-CH2: One of our Austrian clients moved to a cloud accounting platform last year and now wants us to migrate their 12 years of legacy desktop data

content.text: {"expertise":[{"text":"Automated schema drift detection in long-running data pipelines can track field presence probability and distinguish transient field appearances from stable schema additions to reduce false alerts across years of evolving data.","sources":[{"id":"SYN-PUB-06622","field":"abstract","quote":"incremental schema inference engine that updates a probabilistic field model after each observed API response, tracking field presence probability"}]},{"text":"Rule-based frameworks can continuously inspect structured data exports and flag deviations from baseline schemas using declarative specifications, with detection latency under two seconds and false-positive rates below 2.1 percent.","sources":[{"id":"SYN-PUB-06614","field":"abstract","quote":"continuously inspects JSON payloads returned by REST endpoints and flags deviations from a registered baseline schema"}]},{"text":"Data quality monitoring patterns for stream processing pipelines address schema validation and anomaly detection trade-offs including latency impact, fault isolation, and suitability for schema drift detection scenarios.","sources":[{"id":"SYN-PUB-06619","field":"abstract","quote":"embedding schema validation, completeness checks, and anomaly scoring into Kafka consumer and Kafka Streams topologies"}]}],"fit":"strong","fitReason":"The researcher's work on automated schema drift detection [SYN-PUB-06622], rule-based format anomaly detection [SYN-PUB-06614], and data quality monitoring patterns [SYN-PUB-06619] directly addresses the core challenge of detecting and handling format variations across twelve years of legacy data exports with different structures."}
